la:verb:exoro.html:
ex-ōro, āvi, ātum, 1 (archaic
inf. praes. pass. exorarier, ), v. a., to move, prevail upon, persuade by entreaty; to gain or obtain by entreaty (class.): quem ego, ut mentiatur, inducere possum; ut pejeret, exorare facile potero,; cf.: nunc te exoremus necesse est, ut, etc.,: Brutus et Cassius utinam ... per te exorentur, ne, etc., Hirt. ap. : ego patrem exoravi ... tibi ne noceat,: restat Chremes, qui mihi exorandus est,: Ba. Sine te exorem. Ni. Exores tu me? So. Ego quidem ab hoc certe exorabo, ; ; cf.: sine te exorarier,: exorant magnos carmina saepe deos,i. e. soften, appease,: divos (tura),: Lares farre,: populum toties,; cf.: filiae patrem frequentibus litteris,to reconcile the father to the daughter,: aliquem a filii caede precibus,to dissuade,: gnatam ut det, oro, vixque id exoro,I obtain it, prevail,; cf.: res quaedam'st, quam volo Ego me abs te exorare,: quae vicinos concidere loris exorata solet,i. e. although implored, in spite of entreaties,: pacem divum,: amorem,, 11, 43: exoratae arae,.—With quin: numquam edepol quisquam me exorabit, quin eloquar, etc.,.—With double acc.: hanc veniam illis sine te exorem,; cf.: unum exorare vos sinite nos,: unum diem deos,; cf. in the pass.: opem exorata fero,.—Absol.: exorando, haud advorsando sumendam operam censeo,; .

la:verb:exopto.html:
ex-opto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to wish or desire greatly, to long for a thing (class.).
With acc.: quae majori parti pulcherrima videntur, ea maxime exoptant,: Samnitium adventum,: illum exoptavit potius?: aliquid,: omnes te oderunt, tibi pestem exoptant,wish you,.—
With inf.-clause as object: multis de causis te exopto quam primum videre,: aemulari neglegentiam alicuius, (but not in , where the better read. is laudarier optans, v. Vahl. p. 80).—
With ut: omnium hominum exopto ut fiam miserorum miserrimus,: ut sempiternae laudi tibi sit iste tribunatus exopto,.—
Absol.: neque nobis cupientibus atque exoptantibus fructus otii datus est,.—Hence, exoptātus, a, um, P. a., greatly wished or desired, longed for: edepol me uxori exoptatum credo adventurum domum,; ; ; : Antiphila, maxume animo exoptata meo,: ut exoptatum inimico nuntium primus adferret,: erit et tibi exoptatum optinget,; .—Comp.: nihil exoptatius adventu meo,.—Sup.: o mi ere exoptatissume,: gratulatio,.—Adv. seems not to occur.

la:adj:exorabilis.html:
exōrābĭlis, e, adj.
exoro
.
Pass., easily entreated or moved, exorable (class.), : si implacabiles iracundiae sunt, summa est acerbitas: sin autem exorabiles, summa levitas,: in aliquem,: (Orcus) non exorabilis auro,; cf.: nulli exorabilis,: initium vitii,: et exorabile numen fortasse experiar,.— Comp.: in suis quam in alienis exorabilior injuriis,.—*
Act., easily moving, persuasive: carmen,.

la:verb:exorior.gloss: to come out or forth, appear
senses: to come out or forth, appear
la:verb:exorior.html:
ex-ŏrĭor, ortus, 3 and 4 (
part. fut. act. exorturus, —The praes. indic. and imperf. subj. acc. to the third conj.: exoritur,; ; : exoreretur,; cf. ; . —Imper.: exorere,—v. orior), v. dep. n., to come out or forth, to spring up (esp. suddenly, unexpectedly), to rise (class.).
In gen.
Lit.: post solstitium Canicula exoritur,: exoriens sol,; cf.: jubare exorto,: tu sola exorere, quae, etc.,spring up, start up,; cf. ; and .—
Part. praes. subst., exoriens (sc. sol), the rising sun, the morning (very rare): qua venit exoriens, qua deficit, (4, 4, 27 M.).—To designate a cardinal point, the orient, east: plantaria facito ab exoriente,.—
Trop.: exoritur Antipatri ratio ex altera parte,springs, arises,: lex Julia de vi adversus eos exoritur, qui vim commiserint,: ego nunc paulum exorior, et maxime quidem iis litteris, etc.,recover myself,.—
In partic., to arise, proceed, originate, begin, appear, become.
Lit.: (Nilus) exoriens penitus media ab regione diei,arising, proceeding,: e terraque exorta repente arbusta salirent,; cf. : ipse novas assignationes instituit et repentinus Sulla nobis exoritur,arises, appears,; cf.: sic repente anuli beneficio rex exortus est Lydiae (Gyges),became,: exoriare aliquis nostris ex ossibus ultor,.—
Trop.: honestum, quod ex virtutibus exoritur,; cf.: horum (decemvirum) ex injustitia subito exorta est maxima perturbatio,: tot bella repente aliis ex locis exorta sunt,started up, arose, Drak.: a Myrrhina haec sunt exorta omnia,proceeded from, are owing to,: exorti utero dolores,: subito exorta est nefaria Catonis promulgatio,; : id cum contingit, amor exoriatur necesse est,: amicitias exorta aliqua offensione dirumpimus,: exoritur trepidos inter discordia cives,; cf. ; 3, 128: de Praenestinorum defectione fama,

senses: introduction, preface, start or beginning of a speech
la:noun:exordium.html:
exordĭum, ii, n.
exordior, I.
.
Prop., the beginning, the warp of a web (rare): non possum togam praetextam sperare, cum exordium pullum videam,.—
Transf., in gen., a beginning, commencement (the usual meaning; syn.: initium, principium, primordium): neve inde navis inchoandae exordium Coepisset, quae, etc., Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 282 ed. Vahl.): hujus quoque exordium mali, quoniam principium boni diximus, explicemus,; cf.: institutae rei publicae clarum ac tam omnibus notum, id. Rep. 2, 2: a qua totius vitae ducat exor dium,; cf.: a quibus tempo ribus scribendi capiat exordium,: paene ab exordio Urbis,; : tertius (annus) a prima vigilia sumens exordium,.—In plur.: rerum,; ; ; cf. : priva animaï,: solis lunaeque,: rationis,: primae pugnae, et saep.—
In partic., of speech: saepe animadverti, summos oratores in dicendi exordio permoveri,: ergo ita nascetur exordium,—As part of a speech or writing, the introduction, exordium, proëm, preface (syn.: prooemium, praefatio, prologus): exordium est principium orationis, per quod animus auditoris aut judicis constituitur vel apparatur ad audiendum,; cf. : tum denique id, quod primum est dicendum, postremum soleo cogitare, quo utar exordio,: proximus liber a prima parte, id est exordio incipiet,; : in exordio pro Milone,; et saep.— In plur., : quae prima exordia sumat?.—
Transf., a writing, treatise, in gen., ; ;

la:adj:exosus.gloss: hating, loathing, detesting, abhorring ... completely, thoroughly
senses: hating, loathing, detesting, abhorring ... completely, thoroughly
hated, loathed, hateful, odious ... completely, thoroughly
la:adj:exosus.html:
ex-ōsus, a, um, Part. [odi].
Act., hating exceedingly, detesting (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): si nondum exosus ad unum Trojanos,: pugnas,: bella,: terras,: arma,: patrios mores exosus es,: fortunam,.—With gen. (late Lat.): vitae hujus exosa, Boëth. Cons. Phil. 2, 4.—
Pass., hated exceedingly, hateful, odious (post-class.): diis exosos esse,: eo digna omnium ordinum detestatione exoso,; ; : ob scelera universis exosus,: exosum habere, al.

la:verb:exordior.html:
ex-ordĭor, orsus, 4,
v. dep. a., to begin a web, to lay the warp, to weave (class.).
Lit.: funem longum pedes LXXII.,; cf. trop.: neque exordiri primum, unde occipias, habes, Neque detexundam ad telam certos terminos,; and: pertexe modo, Antoni, quod exorsus es,.—
Transf., in gen., to begin, commence, esp. a speech; constr. with the acc., an inf., with ab or absol.
With acc. (so perh. not in Cic.): consilia,: argutias adversus aliquem,: facinus,: hanc rem facete et callide,: bellum ab causa tam nefanda,: classicum ingenti spiritu,: tragoediam magno impetu,: causam,: preces,: parricidia et caedes a Claudio, et saep.—
With inf. (Ciceronian): imitabor ergo Aratum, qui magnis de rebus dicere exordiens, a Jove incipiendum putat,: tunc dicere exorsus est,; cf. ; and —
With ab (class.): aut ab adversarii dicto exordiemur, aut, etc.,: ab ipsa re,: a veritate, a dignitate,.—
Absol. (class.): ancilla hoc pacto exordiri coepit,: jubent exordiri ita, ut eum, qui audiat, benevolum nobis faciamus, etc.,; so, ita, quasi, etc., Quint. prooem. § 4: in hunc modum,: his verbis,: clamore,.!*? exorsus, a, um, in pass. signif., begun, commenced: exorsa tela,; Visell. ap. P.; cf.: reperiunt ea, quibus ante exorsa et potius detexta prope retexantur,.—In the plur. subst.: exorsa, ōrum, n., a beginning, commencement: per ambages et longa exorsa aliquem tenere,a long preamble,: sua cuique exorsa laborem Fortunamque ferent,beginning, undertaking, (opp. exitus), .

la:verb:exonero.html:
ex-ŏnĕro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to free from a burden, to disburden, unload, discharge

(not freq. till after the Aug. per.; in Cic. and Caes. not at all).

Lit.: navem,; Auct. Afr. 8, 1; cf.: navigia jactu,: alvum,; cf. ventrem,; : stomachum nausea gravem,: vesicam,: morbidum corpus (profluvio sanguinis),: velut exoneratus sentinā (nautilus),: nec amnes tantum sed lacus quoque in Padum sese exonerantes,: plenas exonerare colos,to empty, spin off,: ut eam ex hoc exoneres agro,i. e. to send off,; cf.: exonerata plebe coloniis deductis,: multitudo proximas in terras exonerata,.—
Trop., to relieve, free: exonera civitatem vano forsitan metu,; cf.: parte curae senatum,: animum sollicitudine,: exonerata fide mea, quid ultra facere possum, quam uti? etc.,exonerated,: conscientiam suam,: se,: aliquid in quaslibet aures,to confide,; cf.: exonerari laborum meorum partem fateor,is discharged, removed,: dolorem convicio,to vent,: aes alienum,to clear off, pay off,.

la:verb:exorbito.gloss: to go off the track, deviate
senses: to go off the track, deviate
la:verb:exorbito.html:
ex-orbĭto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
[orbita] (post-class.).
Neutr., to go out of the track, to deviate.
Lit.: exorbitantes boves, qui vehiculum trahebant,: stellis exorbitare a praestitutis itineribus non licet,.—
Trop.: a regula,: a catholicae fidei regulis,—
Act., to turn out of the track, turn aside; trop.: animum a tramite,.
la:verb:exorbito.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.

la:verb:exorcizo.gloss: to exorcise: to fend off a demon or a possession through the use of specific prayers
senses: to exorcise: to fend off a demon or a possession through the use of specific prayers
la:verb:exorcizo.html:
exorcīzo, āvi, 1, v. a., = ἐξορκίζω,
to drive away evil spirits by adjuration, to exorcise (post-class.), ; .

la:verb:exorno.html:
ex-orno, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to fit out, equip, furnish, supply with any thing.
In gen. (rare; not in Cic.): nullae magis res duae plus negoti habent (sc. quam navis et mulier) forte si occeperis exornare,to give them an outfit,: dum vicinitatem armis exornat,; so, classem,: aliquem veste, nummis, familia,; cf.: is homo exornetur graphice in peregrinum modum,be fitted out, dressed,: rebus paratis atque exornatis nuptiis,set out, arranged,: convivium omni opulentiā,: aciem,.—Absol.: consul omnibus exploratis, credo dis fretus ... tamen pro rei copia satis providenter exornat,provides, Kritz. —Transf.: hominem exornavit, mulierem qui abduceret,has employed, fitted out, Ritschl N. cr.; cf.: utrum aliquem exornari oportuit, qui istaec prohiberet,—
Pregn., to deck out, adorn, embellish (the class. signif. of the word).
Lit.: ea signa emere soleo, quae ad similitudinem gymnasiorum exornent mihi in palaestra locum,; cf.: domum ejus exornatam atque instructam iste reddiderat nudam atque inanem,: triclinium ample magnificeque,, § 62: aliquem veste regia,: tibi me exorno ut placeam,; cf. ; .—Transf., comically: adeo exornatum dabo, adeo depexum, ut dum vivat, meminerit mei, I'll give him such a dressing, i. e. beating, .—
Trop.: quin tu te exornas moribus lepidis?: Pythagoras exornavit eam Graeciam, quae magna dicta est, praestantissimis artibus,; cf.: philosophiam falsa gloria,; and: L. Fulvius eodem honore (i. e. consulatu) exornatus,: ad illustrandam atque exornandam orationem,; cf.: mea ratio in dicendo haec esse solet, ut boni quod habeat, id amplectar, exornem, exaggerem, etc.,: quid exornamus philosophiam? aut quid ejus nomine gloriosi sumus?set off with praises, extol,.—
To despoil of ornament, . —Hence, exornātus, a, um, P. a., decked out, adorned (rare): candide vestitus, laute exornatusque,: cithara exornatissima,: ornatu nullo potest exornatior esse, Poët. in Anth. Lat. 1, 692 Burm.

la:verb:exolesco.gloss: to grow out, to attain one's full size, grow up
senses: to grow out, to attain one's full size, grow up
to grow to an end, to stop growing
la:verb:exolesco.html:
ex-ŏlesco, olēvi, ētum, 3,
v. inch. n.
To grow out, to attain its full size, grow up.
In gen., so only in the part. perf.exo-letus, a, um, grown up, full grown, mature: exoletus qui excessit olescendi id est crescendi modum, Paul. ex Müll.; cf.: exoletus qui adolescere (olescere?) id est crescere desiit, Müll.: exoleta virgo, P.—
In partic., to denote an abandoned youth of ripe age: scortum exoletum,; cf.: Clodius, qui semper secum scorta, semper exoletos, semper lupas duceret, etc.,; so ; ; ; ; ; ; : remiges,.—
To grow to an end, to stop growing (mostly ante-Aug.; perh. not in Cic.).
Prop.: multa sunt quae neglegentiā exolescunt et fiunt sterilia,; .—
Transf., in gen., to grow out of use, out of date, to become obsolete, to pass away, cease: exolescentes litterae, disappearing, i. e. rubbed off, : ne vetustissima Italiae disciplina per desidiam exolesceret,: rumor validus adeo ut nondum exolescat,: antiquitus instituta,: gratia pascui usu continuo,: cum patris favor haud dum exolevisset,; cf.: nondum is dolor exoleverat,: prima positio vetustate,: exolevit fundendi aeris ratio,: Calchedonii in totum,.—In the part. perf.: scorta,: exoletum jam vetustate odium,; cf. : mos civitatis (with vetus),: et reconditae voces,: auctores,: histrio,.—Absol.: exoleta revocavit, aut etiam nova instituit,.

la:noun:exornatio.html:
exornātĭo, ōnis, f.
exorno
,
an adorning, decorating, embellishing.
Lit.: quae ad lavationem, quae ad exornationem pertinerent, to the toilet, Col. (Cic. Oecon.?) 12, 3, 2.—
Trop., of speech, embellishment.
In gen.: ipsa inventa exponentur simpliciter sine ulla exornatione (corresp. to expolitio),: verborum et sententiarum,.—
In partic., as a figure of speech., Auct. Her.
